slides.texte_overlay:
Things men learn too
late about friendship
Friendships fade quietly, not with a fight. No drama, just months without a call. If you value someone, put a regular dinner or call in the calendar.
The friends from your 20s won't all stay. People move, marry, change. Keeping a few close is a choice you make again and again, not something that just happens.
Men need to talk too. Not just about football and work. A friend who asks "How are you really?" and waits for the answer is worth more than ten party friends.
You can make new friends at any age. A sport, a class, a new job. It feels awkward at first, but adult friendships can be the deepest ones of all.
Before: catch-ups were the same old stories. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and something new to bring to every dinner with friends.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: catch-ups were the same old stories. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Now I bring something new to every dinner.

slides.texte_overlay: Showing up matters more than saying the right thing. At the hospital, the funeral, the move. You don't need words. Being there is the whole message.
Real friends are allowed to disagree with you. The one who tells you a hard truth kindly is protecting you. Keep that friend close for the rest of your life.
